what_happened: The GitHub Pages deploy for PR #76 timed out on GitHub's side. Athena has no step that watches or retries its deploy, so the operator reran it by hand. The rerun was cancelled too. The next push deployed the site.
cause: Athena treats a merge as finished once it is pushed. It does not own the post-merge deploy as part of the outcome. Nothing checks that the published site matches the merged change, so a transient failure on the hosting side goes unnoticed until a human sees it. A one-off manual rerun also has no standing rule for how to handle a stuck or cancelled deploy.
prevention: After a merge that triggers a Pages deploy, add a step that polls the deploy workflow run to a final state. On failure, timeout or cancellation it should rerun automatically, with a bounded number of attempts and backoff. If the deploy is still not green after those attempts, it should report the job as not done and name the run, instead of leaving the operator to find it. Success should also confirm that the live site serves the merged commit. This covers every transient external deploy failure, not only Pages.
proposed_request: After Athena merges a change that triggers a GitHub Pages deploy, make Athena watch the deploy run until it reaches a final state. If the run fails, times out or is cancelled, Athena should rerun it automatically, up to 3 attempts with increasing waits. It should count the job as done only when the deploy succeeds and the live site serves the merged commit. If the deploy still fails after the retries, Athena should report the job as not done, with a link to the failed run, so the operator is told instead of finding it later. Check this against the PR #76 case: a deploy that times out on GitHub's side should be retried without anyone touching it.
